log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Floette
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Scrafty
Floette used Light of Ruin → Gholdengo
Floette used Light of Ruin → Gholdengo
Floette used Light of Ruin → Gholdengo

decisions.rationale: Lead Tyranitar+Excadrill sand core: Excadrill (Sand Rush, 154→308 in sand) outspeeds the entire opponent roster, is immune to Garchomp Earthquake, and threatens Floette with Iron Head SE. Tyranitar sets sand automatically and provides Rock Slide spread pressure. Back: Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag wincon, 178 Spe outspeeds most of the meta) and Gholdengo (Steel typing resists Floette Fairy, Make It Rain spread, Good as Gold blocks Taunt/status). This covers opponent's likely Milotic/Scrafty adjustments—Gholdengo walls Scrafty's Drain Punch via Steel resist and Gengar-Mega is immune to it; Excadrill under sand outspeeds Milotic's Icy Wind speed control. Only real concern is Talonflame Gale Wings Tailwind giving Garchomp 268-338 Spe, but Protect scouting and sand chip vs Focus Sash mitigate this.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Leading Tyranitar+Excadrill sand core, Gengar+Gholdengo in back. Opponent lost G1 with Garchomp/Talonflame/Metagross/Floette-Mega; expect Milotic or Scrafty adjustment. Key threats: (1) Talonflame Gale Wings Tailwind gives Garchomp 268-338 Spe, outspeeding Excadrill in sand (308) and Gengar-Mega (178)—Protect scout turn 1 if Talonflame lead detected; (2) Milotic Competitive punishes Intimidate users (Grimmsnarl/Tauros not brought this game); (3) Scrafty Intimidate+Snarl disrupts both physical and special attackers—Gholdengo resists Drain Punch, Gengar-Mega immune. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is wincon: bring it when opponent has 2+ mons remaining to trap. Floette-Mega Light of Ruin OHKOs Tyranitar—keep Tyranitar away from Floette if possible, or use Excadrill Iron Head SE to force it out. Excadrill is immune to Earthquake (Ground/Steel) so safe alongside Tyranitar vs Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Lead Scrafty + Milotic to disrupt the sand opener with Intimidate/Fake Out pressure while Milotic attacks Excadrill; retain Garchomp and Floette for the midgame after Excadrill is controlled.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's observed game-1 four were Tyranitar, Excadrill, Leftovers Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar, with Tyranitar–Excadrill as a sand lead. Prioritize removing or denying Excadrill before exposing Mega Floette; sand invalidates reliance on Talonflame's Focus Sash.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill Protects to waste Scrafty's likely Fake Out (standard turn-1 play, most likely targeting Excadrill at 308 Spe). Tyranitar Crunches Milotic for 21–41% neutral damage plus 20% Def-drop chance, targeting the bigger threat (Scald is SE vs both my mons). Milotic likely Scalds Tyranitar for 30–44% which it survives comfortably. Risk: Scrafty could Drain Punch Tyranitar (70–106%, possible OHKO), but Fake Out is the standard play and Excadrill is the natural target. This preserves Excadrill at 100% and chips Milotic for turn 2.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 T1: Led Ttar+Exca vs Scrafty+Milotic. Scrafty Intimidate hit both at -1 Atk. Key damage benchmarks: Scrafty Drain Punch vs Ttar 70-106% (possible OHKO 4x SE), vs Exca 62-96%; Milotic Scald vs Ttar 30-44%, vs Exca 68-103% (possible OHKO, Sash saves); Ttar Crunch vs Milotic 21-41%; Exca HH vs Milotic 23-43%. Scrafty Fake Out is NVE 0.5x vs both. Plan: Protect Exca T1 to waste FO, chip Milotic with Ttar. T2: Exca HH or Rock Slide depending on board. Keep Ttar away from Floette-Mega (Light of Ruin OHKOs). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is late-game wincon. Gholdengo resists Scald (Steel) and is immune to Drain Punch (Ghost).

decisions.rationale: Deny Excadrill’s immediate Sand Rush attack with Fake Out while Scald applies major damage and a burn chance; this most directly limits the sand lead’s pressure before bringing Floette in.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s observed game-1 four were Tyranitar, Focus Sash Excadrill, Leftovers Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar. Prioritize denying or removing Sand Rush Excadrill before exposing Mega Floette; sand makes Talonflame’s Focus Sash unreliable.

decisions.rationale: Switch Tyranitar to Gholdengo to escape the 4x SE Drain Punch KO range (70-106%); Gholdengo is immune to Drain Punch (Ghost) and can Recover off Scald damage. Excadrill at 308 Speed moves first and lands High Horsepower into Milotic (34-64% of max HP), bringing it to ~11-41% before it can be KO'd. This preserves Tyranitar for late-game, maximizes Excadrill's Sash value by getting damage off first, and brings in a safe Gholdengo that threatens Make It Rain / Shadow Ball against the weakened foe field.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 T2: Switched Ttar→Gholdengo to escape Drain Punch KO range; Exca HH into Milotic (34-64%). Milotic +2 SpA Scald OHKOs Exca through Sash (136-203%); Scrafty Drain Punch 4x SE vs Ttar possible OHKO (70-106%). Gholdengo immune to Drain Punch (Ghost). Milotic Scald vs Gholdengo 51-76% (tool says neutral, not 0.5x). Gholdengo resists Scald in standard chart but tool reports neutral—trust tool. Plan: chip down Milotic, keep Ttar away from Scrafty Drain Punch, save Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag for late-game. Floette-Mega Light of Ruin OHKOs Ttar—keep Ttar away. Gholdengo Make It Rain good vs Scrafty (Dark/Fighting neutral to Steel but spread chip).

decisions.rationale: Split pressure: Drain Punch heavily damages Tyranitar while +2 Scald can remove or force Focus Sash on Sand Rush Excadrill, setting up cleanup next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has shown Focus Sash Sand Rush Excadrill and Smooth Rock Tyranitar; prioritize removing or breaking Excadrill before committing Mega Floette. Game 1’s observed remaining members were Leftovers Gholdengo and Mega Gengar.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Milotic with Excadrill HH (308 Spe, moves first) + Gholdengo Shadow Ball to guarantee KO (combined 60-109% vs 35% HP). Removing +2 SpA Milotic is top priority. Shadow Ball chosen over Make It Rain to avoid self-SpA-drop (would be -2 with Snarl) and deal more to Milotic. Excadrill is at 1% and dies anyway, so spending its last action to help KO Milotic is optimal. If Milotic Protects, Excadrill is lost (1% anyway) but Gholdengo stays healthy for Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag late-game.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 T3: Double-targeted Milotic with Exca HH + Gholdengo Shadow Ball to remove +2 SpA threat. Exca at 1% is expendable. Gholdengo Shadow Ball > Make It Rain for Milotic KO reliability and SpA preservation (avoid -2 from Make It Rain + Snarl). Plan: bring in Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag next turn to trap remaining foes. Keep Ttar away from Scrafty Drain Punch (4x SE) and Floette-Mega Light of Ruin. Snarl only does 12-23% to Gholdengo — manageable. Scrafty Drain Punch heals it significantly if it KOs Exca.

decisions.rationale: Send in Gengar to Mega Evolve into Shadow Tag, trapping both Milotic (35% HP, +2 SpA) and Scrafty (82% HP). Gengar-Mega outspeeds both foes and is unaffected by Intimidate. Tyranitar is 4x weak to Scrafty Drain Punch and would be Intimidated on entry, making it a poor choice. Shadow Tag prevents the opponent from switching Milotic out to preserve the +2 SpA threat or to bring in a counter.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 plan: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag traps both foes. Priority: KO Milotic (35%, +2 SpA) first with Gholdengo Shadow Ball + Gengar Shadow Ball. Then trap and wear down Scrafty with Sludge Bomb (SE vs Fighting). Keep Ttar away from Scrafty Drain Punch (4x SE). Snarl does only 12-23% to Gholdengo — manageable. Gholdengo at -1 SpA from Snarl; consider Recover if needed. Opponent has 2 unrevealed Pokemon; Shadow Tag prevents them from coming in until a current foe faints.

decisions.rationale: Protect Milotic from Excadrill’s immediate Sand Rush pressure while Snarl covers an Excadrill Protect attempt, removes Excadrill if it attacks, and weakens Gholdengo for the following turns.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s confirmed Game 2 core includes Focus Sash Sand Rush Excadrill, Smooth Rock Sand Stream Tyranitar, and Leftovers Gholdengo. Game 1 revealed Mega Gengar as a likely remaining option. Preserve answers to Gholdengo and avoid exposing Mega Floette into Steel pressure prematurely.

decisions.rationale: Double Shadow Ball into Milotic guarantees a KO (combined min ~40.6% > 35% HP) while Mega Evolving Gengar activates Shadow Tag to trap both foes. Gengar-Mega (Speed 200) outspeeds Milotic and hits first with boosted SpA 222 Shadow Ball; Gholdengo cleans up. Milotic's Protect has reduced success rate from last-turn use, and even if it Recovers between hits, Shadow Tag prevents escape and we finish next turn. This removes the +2 SpA Milotic threat immediately and locks Scrafty in for Sludge Bomb next phase.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega now active with Shadow Tag (SpA 222, Spe 200). Plan: KO Milotic this turn with double Shadow Ball. Next: trap Scrafty and wear down with Sludge Bomb (SE vs Fighting, 29.7-53.6% pre-Mega, higher post-Mega; Roseli Berry already factored). Gholdengo at -1 SpA (may drop to -2 from Snarl); use Recover if below 40%. Keep Tyranitar away from Scrafty (Drain Punch 4x SE). Opponent has 2 unrevealed from {Floette-Eternal, Garchomp, Talonflame, Metagross} — Shadow Tag prevents them entering until a current foe faints. Series score 1-0; winning this game closes the series 2-0.

decisions.rationale: Preserve boosted Milotic from likely focused special damage while bringing Garchomp in safely; Snarl immediately suppresses both special attackers and compounds Gholdengo’s existing Special Attack drop.

Gengar-Mega outspeeds Garchomp (200 vs 134-169) and Shadow Ball KOs it at 10% before Earthquake can fire (which would guarantee-KO Gengar and possibly Gholdengo). Gholdengo Protects to dodge Scrafty's Snarl (17-32% to Gengar, survivable) and avoid dropping to -3 SpA, staying fresh for the 4th foe arriving after Garchomp faints. Next turn: Taunt Scrafty to lock it out of Snarl/Protect, then wear it down with Sludge Bomb while handling the new entrant.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 plan after Garchomp KO: Gengar-Mega Taunt locks Scrafty (only Drain Punch left, immune to Ghosts). Then Sludge Bomb SE vs Scrafty Fighting typing. Gholdengo at -2 SpA should Recover if below 40% or support with chip. Watch for 4th foe: Floette-Eternal (Moonblast SE vs Gengar, Floettite Mega), Talonflame (Gale Wings priority Brave Bird, Focus Sash), or Metagross (Clear Body, Lum Berry, Bullet Punch priority). Shadow Tag traps all foes on field. Series 1-0; winning this game closes 2-0.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Garchomp through the immediate double-target threat while Snarl further suppresses both special attackers for the Milotic/Floette endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s confirmed Game 2 core includes Focus Sash Sand Rush Excadrill, Smooth Rock Sand Stream Tyranitar, Leftovers Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar. Preserve answers to Gholdengo and avoid exposing Mega Floette into Steel pressure prematurely; stack special-attack drops from Scrafty when Mega Gengar and Gholdengo are paired.

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega (200 Spe) outspeeds and guaranteed-KOs Garchomp (10% HP) with Shadow Ball before it can Earthquake, which would KO Gengar (121-173%) and possibly Gholdengo (72-105%). Gholdengo Shadow Balls Scrafty for safe 7-14% chip (NVE but guaranteed progress) rather than risking a reduced-success-rate Protect or wasting Recover at 92%. Next turn Gengar Taunts Scrafty, locking it to Drain Punch (immune to both Ghosts) and neutralizing it while we handle the 4th foe under Shadow Tag.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Garchomp KO'd turn 6 by Gengar Shadow Ball. Next: Gengar Taunt on Scrafty locks it to Drain Punch (immune to Ghosts), making it a dead slot. Both my Pokémon at -2 SpA (will be -3 after Snarl). 4th foe unknown: Floette-Eternal (Moonblast SE vs Gengar, Floettite Mega), Talonflame (Gale Wings BB SE vs Gengar, Focus Sash), or Metagross (Clear Body, Lum Berry, Bullet Punch). Tyranitar fresh at 100% on bench for sand refresh and physical damage if SpA drops become crippling. Shadow Tag traps all foes. Series 1-0; winning this game = 2-0 sweep.

decisions.rationale: Preserve the 11% Garchomp by switching to Milotic; Snarl further suppresses both special attackers while Milotic is the safer pivot into their reduced-power attacks.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 2 core confirmed: Smooth Rock Sand Stream Tyranitar, Focus Sash Sand Rush Excadrill, Leftovers Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar. Against Mega Gengar plus Gholdengo, prioritize repeated Snarl special-attack drops and preserve Milotic as the stable special-pressure pivot; avoid exposing Mega Floette to Steel/Poison pressure before those attackers are controlled.

decisions.rationale: Snarl maintains special-attack pressure while Earthquake is the only available Garchomp action that can immediately remove Mega Gengar and heavily punish Gholdengo if an opening arises.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag can trap active grounded allies; against its Gholdengo pairing, continue prioritizing Snarl special-attack drops and preserve Milotic as the stable special-pressure pivot. Avoid exposing Mega Floette to Steel- and Poison-type pressure before those attackers are controlled.

decisions.rationale: Bring in Milotic: it is the safest pivot into the heavily reduced special attackers and preserves Floette-Eternal from immediate Steel- and Poison-type pressure.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar is extremely fast and its Shadow Tag traps grounded active Pokémon. Against Gholdengo plus Mega Gengar, repeated Snarl is valuable for suppressing both special attackers; preserve Milotic as the durable special-pressure pivot and avoid exposing Mega Floette until Steel- and Poison-type pressure is controlled.

decisions.rationale: Both my Pokémon are at -3 SpA, making special attacks useless (Gholdengo Shadow Ball does only 11-18% to Milotic, can't KO). Switch Gholdengo to Tyranitar for physical damage (unaffected by SpA drops), sand refresh via Sandstream+Smooth Rock (8 turns), and Snarl immunity in practice (NVE 0.5x, only 1.4-3.4% damage). Gengar Protects to avoid potential KO from Scrafty's Snarl (17.5-32.1% vs 27% HP = possible KO) and preserves Shadow Tag, preventing the opponent from switching to their unknown 4th Pokémon. Next turn: Tyranitar Rock Slide both foes while Gengar Taunts Scrafty to lock out Protect.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Both special attackers at -3 SpA from repeated Snarls — special damage is negligible. Tyranitar is the win condition: physical attacker, Sandstream+Smooth Rock for 8-turn sand, Snarl NVE (0.5x). Plan: Tyranitar Rock Slide spreads damage to both trapped foes; Gengar Taunt on Scrafty prevents Protect (Scrafty can still Snarl but it's NVE on Tyranitar and Gengar can Protect-cycle). Milotic at 35% with Competitive +2 SpA is the main threat to Tyranitar (Scald SE). 4th foe unknown: Floette-Eternal (Moonblast SE vs Gengar, Mega), Talonflame (Gale Wings BB SE vs Gengar, Sash), or Metagross (Clear Body, Lum, Bullet Punch). Shadow Tag must stay active to prevent foe switching. Series 1-0; winning this game = 2-0 sweep.

decisions.rationale: Snarl plus Scald guarantees the Mega Gengar KO if it does not Protect while further suppressing both special attackers; their heavily reduced damage makes proactive removal better than Recover.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar is Timid, extremely fast, and Shadow Tag traps grounded actives. Gholdengo is Modest with Leftovers and Good as Gold. Repeated Snarl is the central endgame tool against their special-attacking core; preserve Floette until Gholdengo and Mega Gengar are controlled. Tyranitar has Smooth Rock Sand Stream and physical Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect.

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar must Protect: Scrafty Drain Punch does 69.6-106.3% (4x SE, potential KO from 98%) and Milotic Scald does 30-44.4% (2x SE, +2 Competitive). The opponent's optimal play is double-targeting Tyranitar to KO the win condition. Protect guarantees survival. Gengar at 21% will die to Snarl+sand regardless, so instead of a reduced-success Protect it should Taunt Milotic (guaranteed to move first at 200 Spe vs 78-110). Taunt locks Milotic out of Recover/Protect for 3 turns, stranding it at 35% HP. If opponent double-targets Tyranitar (most likely), both attacks are blocked and Gengar survives unharmed with Milotic Taunted — best outcome. If Scrafty Snarls instead, Gengar dies but Milotic is still Taunted. Sandstorm ends after this turn, preserving Tyranitar as the healthy win condition going forward.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 ongoing, series 1-0. Opponent roster: Garchomp (Jolly, Life Orb, Rough Skin) fainted; Milotic (Bold, Leftovers, Competitive, +2 SpA from Crunch def drop); Scrafty (Careful, Roseli Berry, Intimidate); 4th unknown among Floette-Eternal (Timid, Floettite, Flower Veil), Talonflame (Jolly, Focus Sash, Gale Wings), Metagross (Adamant, Lum Berry, Clear Body). Key damage benchmarks: Scrafty Drain Punch 69.6-106.3% to Tyranitar (4x SE); Milotic Scald 30-44.4% to Tyranitar (2x SE +2 Competitive); Snarl ~19% to Gengar-Mega each use; Tyranitar Crunch 31.7-60% to Milotic (neutral); Tyranitar Rock Slide 22.3-42.4% to Milotic (possible KO from 35%), 11-20% to Scrafty (NVE). Sandstorm (Smooth Rock 8 turns) ends turn 8. Win condition: Tyranitar physical attacker chips down trapped foes; Gengar Shadow Tag must stay active as long as possible. If Gengar faints, opponent can switch 4th Pokemon in. Gholdengo (86%, Modest, Leftovers, Good as Gold) is benched with Recover; immune to Drain Punch (Ghost) but SE-weak to Snarl.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Scald guarantees the Mega Gengar KO if it does not land its reduced-success consecutive Protect, while Drain Punch gives the best Tyranitar pressure and recovery.

Milotic is Taunted at 41% HP and cannot Protect or Recover — this is the optimal turn to guarantee her KO. Crunch (31.7-60%, 100% acc) + Shadow Ball (25.7-44.7%, 100% acc) = 57.4% minimum combined, guaranteed KO from 41%. Tyranitar is almost certainly dying to Drain Punch+Scald (99.6% min combined) regardless of our choice, so maximizing value by removing Milotic is paramount. Protect is only ~50% reliable and doesn't pressure Milotic; Rock Slide risks 10% miss. With Milotic gone, Gholdengo (immune to Drain Punch) faces only Scrafty+4th, and can Recover-stall while chipping with Shadow Ball. If Tyranitar somehow survives (opponent mispredicts), we keep a 98% Tyranitar for next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 turn 9: series 1-0. Gengar and Excadrill fainted; Tyranitar (98%, -1 SpA) and Gholdengo (86%, -1 SpA) remain vs Scrafty (50%) + Milotic (41%, Taunted through ~turn 10-11) + unknown 4th. Shadow Tag gone (Gengar dead) so opponent can switch freely. Milotic Competitive +2 SpA resets on switch-in; current Milotic switched in turn 6 so stat boosts reset. Sandstorm ended turn 8. Key: Milotic Taunted = must attack (Scald/Icy Wind only). Scrafty Drain Punch 4x SE on Tyranitar (69.6-106.3%). If Tyranitar falls, Gholdengo must handle Scrafty (immune to Drain Punch, weak to Snarl) + 4th. Floette-Eternal/Talonflame/Metagross all unknown. For game 3 if needed: opponent tends to lead Scrafty+Milotic with Intimidate+Competitive synergy; Garchomp is Life Orb Jolly Rough Skin. Consider preserving Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag longer in future games.

decisions.rationale: Snarl further suppresses Gholdengo while Scald makes substantial progress on Tyranitar; this preserves the strongest stable endgame against their special attacker.
decisions.notebook: Repeated Snarl is the key endgame tool versus Gholdengo; avoid exposing Floette until Steel pressure is sufficiently controlled.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Tyranitar is guaranteed KO'd by Floette's Light of Ruin or Scrafty's Drain Punch if it doesn't Protect, and Floette outspeeds it so it can't even attack first. Protect Tyranitar to waste the opponent's likely Tyranitar-targeted moves. Gholdengo Make It Rain hits both foes for 43-74% on Floette (2x SE) and 22-39% on Scrafty (neutral), putting both in KO range next turn. Even if Scrafty predicts and Snarls Gholdengo instead, damage is only 12-23% and Gholdengo survives comfortably.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 turn 10: series 1-0. Floette-Eternal holds Floettite (Mega Stone) but Mega form stats unknown. Floette outspeeds both my Pokémon (123-158 vs Tyranitar 81, Gholdengo 104). Light of Ruin guaranteed KO on Tyranitar at 48%. Scrafty Drain Punch guaranteed KO on Tyranitar. All Floette moves 0.5x on Gholdengo. Make It Rain at -1 SpA does 43-74% to Floette, 22-39% to Scrafty. Make It Rain drops SpA by 1 on use (Gholdengo would go to -2). For game 3 if needed: opponent leads Scrafty+Milotic with Intimidate+Competitive synergy; Garchomp Life Orb Jolly. Consider preserving Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag longer. Floette-Eternal is Timid 123-158 Speed with Moonblast/Light of Ruin/Energy Ball/Protect.

decisions.rationale: Mega Moonblast secures Tyranitar while Snarl further suppresses Gholdengo; it also covers a Tyranitar Protect by still lowering Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette has Fairy Aura and substantially higher Special Attack/Speed; use Mega Moonblast to reliably remove Tyranitar. Repeated Snarl is the key endgame tool versus Gholdengo; avoid exposing Floette until Steel pressure is sufficiently controlled.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Tyranitar is guaranteed KO'd by Floette this turn. Protect (reduced rate) is the only way Tyranitar can possibly survive — if it works and only Floette targets Tyranitar (likely, since Scrafty at 27% may Protect or Snarl Gholdengo rather than waste Drain Punch on a potential Protect), Tyranitar lives at 48% and can Ice Punch the chipped Scrafty next turn for a guaranteed KO. Gholdengo's Make It Rain chips both foes critically: Scrafty to 7-16% (KO range next turn) and Floette to 66-82%. Even if Tyranitar dies as expected, the chip damage is essential for Gholdengo's endgame path — it resists all Floette moves at 0.5x and has Recover/Leftovers to outlast a 1v1. The SpA drop to -6 is acceptable since Gholdengo's damage is already minimal and the chip is what matters.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 turn 11: series 1-0. Make It Rain drops SpA by 2 stages in this format (confirmed from stat tracking). Floette-Mega Light of Ruin does 42.8-59.3% to Gholdengo even at 0.5x — extremely powerful, be wary. Floette-Mega Speed confirmed 134-169, outspeeds Gholdengo (104) and Tyranitar (81). Scrafty Speed 78-110 (Careful). For game 3 if needed: opponent brings Scrafty+Milotic with Intimidate+Competitive synergy; Garchomp Life Orb Jolly. Consider preserving Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag longer — trap and eliminate Floette or Milotic early. Lead Gengar-Mega + Excadrill to threaten both Floette (Shadow Ball) and Milotic (High Horsepower) under Shadow Tag. Opponent's full roster: Garchomp (LO, Jolly, Rough Skin), Milotic (Leftovers, Bold, Competitive), Scrafty (Roseli Berry, Careful, Intimidate), Floette-Mega (Floettite, Timid, Fairy Aura, moves Moonblast/LightofRuin/EnergyBall/Protect), Talonflame (FocusSash, Jolly, GaleWings), Metagross (LumBerry, Adamant, ClearBody).

decisions.rationale: Moonblast is a guaranteed KO on Tyranitar if it does not Protect, while Snarl further suppresses Gholdengo’s already heavily reduced Special Attack and advances the safe endgame.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette’s Fairy Aura Moonblast reliably threatens Tyranitar; Scrafty Snarl is the core answer to Gholdengo, whose Special Attack can be reduced repeatedly while Leftovers recovery is managed.

decisions.rationale: Gholdengo is in a 1v2 at 59% HP with SpA at -6 (floor). Floette outspeeds and Light of Ruin can KO from 59% (42.8-59.3%). Make It Rain only max-rolls to KO Scrafty (8.7-15% vs 15% HP) and Recover risks death before healing. Protect (+4 priority) guarantees survival, wastes both foes' attacks, and Leftovers heals to ~65%. Up 1-0 in the series, no need to coin-flip Gholdengo's life — stall for an opening next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 turn 12: Gholdengo 1v2 vs Scrafty(15%)+Floette-Mega(72%), SpA at -6 floor. Make It Rain does 8.7-15% to Scrafty (only max roll KOs at 15% HP) and 14.4-25.5% to Floette. Floette Light of Ruin can KO Gholdengo from 59% (42.8-59.3%, 90% acc). Moonblast does 28.9-40.2%. Scrafty Snarl does 12.4-22.7%. All Floette attacks NVE vs Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost). Scrafty Drain Punch immune to Gholdengo. For game 3: lead Gengar-Mega+Excadrill to trap and eliminate Floette or Milotic early under Shadow Tag; preserve Gengar longer. Opponent brings Scrafty+Milotic with Intimidate+Competitive synergy; Garchomp LO Jolly. Consider Protect-stall cycles with Gholdengo when at SpA floor to bait opponent misplays.

decisions.rationale: Light of Ruin is the only available attack with a direct KO chance on the weakened Gholdengo before it can Recover; Snarl adds damage if it attacks rather than recovering and maintains special-pressure control.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette is faster than opposing Gholdengo and Fairy Aura-boosted Light of Ruin is the key high-damage option into it. Scrafty Snarl is the core answer to Gholdengo, whose Special Attack can be reduced repeatedly while Leftovers recovery is managed.

decisions.rationale: Recover is the safest survival play. Floette-Mega outspeeds and hits first, but Light of Ruin (max 59.3%) cannot KO Gholdengo from 65% alone. If Scrafty is slower than Gholdengo (uncertain 78-110 vs 104), Recover resolves before Snarl, guaranteeing survival at 33-60% HP. If Scrafty is faster, the KO risk is the same as Make It Rain, but Recover at least heals if I survive. If opponent uses Moonblast (100% acc, 28.9-40.2%) instead of Light of Ruin to avoid recoil, combined with Snarl (12.4-22.7%) = 41.3-62.9% < 65%, guaranteeing survival and healing to near full. Make It Rain only KOs Scrafty on max roll (~5%) and always eats both hits first. Protect is unreliable after last turn. Recover keeps me alive to chip with Make It Rain on future turns while Floette's Light of Ruin recoil slowly self-damages, potentially bringing Floette into KO range.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 turn 13: Gholdengo 1v2 at 65% HP, SpA -6 floor. Recover chosen to maximize survival. Light of Ruin max 59.3% cannot solo KO from 65%. Scrafty speed uncertain (78-110 vs Gholdengo 104). Floette Light of Ruin has 90% acc + 50% recoil — each use chips Floette significantly (~26-36% of its HP). Path to win: stall with Recover, chip with Make It Rain when safe, exploit Light of Ruin recoil to bring Floette into KO range. If game 2 lost, series goes to game 3 tied 1-1. Game 3 plan: lead Gengar-Mega+Excadrill, Shadow Tag trap to eliminate Floette or Milotic early, preserve Gengar longer. Opponent likely brings Scrafty+Milotic (Intimidate+Competitive synergy) or Scrafty+Floette-Mega. Watch for Scrafty speed investment — range 78-110 suggests possible speed creeping past 104.

decisions.rationale: Apply maximum immediate combined pressure: Light of Ruin has the best KO chance at this range, while Snarl adds crucial damage and keeps Gholdengo’s Special Attack suppressed.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette outspeeds opposing Gholdengo; Fairy Aura-boosted Light of Ruin plus Scrafty Snarl is the primary route to break it. Repeated Snarl drops make Gholdengo’s special attacks far less threatening.

decisions.rationale: Floette outspeeds Gholdengo and Light of Ruin (42.8-59.3%) likely KOs from 46% before Gholdengo can act. Floette would self-KO from recoil at 36% HP, but the opponent wins anyway since Scrafty survives at 15%. Protect is the only safe play: blocks Light of Ruin + Snarl, wastes Floette's limited PP, and Leftovers heals to ~52%. Gholdengo can stall out Light of Ruin PP (likely 3 left) with 6 Protect PP, then out-heal NVE Moonblast/Energy Ball with Recover while Scrafty's Snarl PP also depletes. Any non-Protect play risks ~65% instant game loss.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 plan: Lead Gengar-Mega+Excadrill, Shadow Tag trap to eliminate Floette or Milotic early, preserve Gengar longer. reflections.summary: Scrafty's Snarl was super-effective against both Gengar and Gholdengo, repeatedly dropping their SpA while chipping them down. By the time Floette-Mega arrived, Gholdengo's SpA was -6 (Snarl + Make It Rain self-drops stacked), making it unable to threaten anything. Tyranitar also carelessly Crunched Milotic, triggering Competitive (+2 SpA). Gengar-Mega never trapped anything useful and died to Scald after being worn down by Snarl. Floette-Mega swept the helpless endgame.
reflections.adjustment: Never let Gengar or Gholdengo sit in against Scrafty — Snarl is SE on both and destroys their offense. Use Gengar's Taunt on Scrafty to shut down Snarl, or pivot to Tyranitar/Excadrill to hit Scrafty with physical attacks. Stop using Make It Rain once SpA drops begin accumulating. Do not use stat-lowering moves on Milotic (Competitive). Prioritize trapping Floette with Shadow Tag before it Mega Evolves and sweeps.
reflections.notebook: Game 3 plan: Lead Gengar-Mega + Excadrill. Use Taunt on Scrafty turn 1 to block Snarl — this is the single highest priority adjustment. If Scrafty is present, never leave Gengar/Gholdengo in without Taunt active. Target Scrafty with physical attacks (Excadrill High Horsepower, Tyranitar Crunch is fine on Scrafty) to remove it before special attackers need to operate. Avoid any stat-lowering move on Milotic (Competitive +2 SpA). If Floette is on the field unevolved, trap with Shadow Tag and KO immediately before Fairy Aura activates. Key durable facts: (1) Scrafty Snarl is SE vs Gengar AND Gholdengo — the core matchup problem; Scrafty speed ≥104 (outspeeds or ties Gholdengo). (2) Scrafty Roseli Berry still intact (never triggered) — weakens first SE Fairy hit. (3) Floette-Mega Light of Ruin: 140 BP Fairy Aura-boosted, 90% acc, 50% recoil; does ~50% to Gholdengo even NVE; Moonblast OHKO'd Tyranitar (SE). (4) Make It Rain self-SpA-drop compounds catastrophically with Snarl — avoid stacking. (5) Milotic Competitive + Intimidate synergy is dangerous; Taunt shuts down Recover/Protect but do not use stat-lowering attacks on it. (6) Talonflame (Gale Wings, Focus Sash, Jolly) and Metagross (Clear Body, Lum Berry, Adamant) still not brought through 2 games — expect one or both game 3. (7) Garchomp brought game 2 (Life Orb, Rough Skin, Jolly) — may rotate out game 3. (8) Consider Gholdengo as late-game cleaner only after Scrafty is removed; otherwise it gets walled to -6 SpA.

reflections.summary: Won by bringing the right four—Scrafty, Milotic, Garchomp, and Mega Floette—and using Scrafty’s repeated Snarl to suppress the opponent’s Mega Gengar/Gholdengo special core. Mega Floette was the correct evolution and gave the decisive Gholdengo endgame pressure with Fairy Aura-boosted Light of Ruin. Piloting was mostly solid, though Drain Punch into the newly revealed Gholdengo on turn 2 wasted Scrafty’s action.
reflections.adjustment: When Gholdengo is on the field, prioritize Snarl rather than Drain Punch: it deals effective spread damage, lowers its Special Attack, and avoids its Ghost-type immunity. Keep Mega Floette preserved for the weakened-Gholdengo endgame.
